candidates.summary: A same-depth tie no longer returns early, so the walk goes on into later siblings and marks their types in the shared guard set; the parent's own shallower embed of one of those types is then pruned, and a Go-valid program that the base accepted is now rejected at preprocess
candidates.failure_scenario: T{S; R}, S{A; B; Z}, Z{R}; A, B and R each define M; var i I = T{}. Go resolves T.M to R.M at depth 1, and go/types accepts it. The base returned nil from S at the A/B conflict before it visited Z, so T then found R.M and the program printed R.M. At head, S records the A/B tie and keeps walking into Z, which marks R visited. T's direct R embed is then pruned, so preprocess panics with 'main.T does not implement main.I (missing method M)'. AddPackage (keeper.go:647) and MsgRun (keeper.go:1030) type-check with go/types first, so a package of this shape clears the gate and then fails in the VM. That is the deploy-gate-bypass class the ADR says this change closes, reopened for a shape the base handled correctly. It contradicts the ADR's 'zero-regression' and 'no longer panic at VM preprocess' lines.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/solo-finder-1-tiewalk.gno gnovm/tests/files/solo1_tiewalk.gno; cd gnovm/pkg/gnolang && go test -run 'TestFiles/solo1_tiewalk' -v . at head (expect FAIL: does not implement) and with base types.go checked out (expect PASS, R.M); go run the Go twin (prints R.M)
candidates.evidence: head: 'unexpected panic: main/solo1_tiewalk.gno:35:6-15: main.T does not implement main.I (missing method M)', FAIL. base c775354dd types.go: '--- PASS: TestFiles/solo1_tiewalk.gno'. Go twin: 'R.M', exit 0. The base run reported no TypeCheckError diff, so go/types accepts it.

candidates.summary: A subtree now returns its shallowest candidate even after its deeper path has consumed a type that the parent embeds directly; the parent's shallower embed is pruned, so the selector silently resolves to a different method than Go picks, where the base rejected
candidates.failure_scenario: T{S; R}, S{C; X}, X{R}; C and R each define M; R carries a field V. Go resolves t.M() and i.M() to R.M on t.R at depth 1, prints 'R.M outer', and go/types accepts it. The base saw C.M and X.R.M inside S as a conflict, returned nil, and found R already visited, so it rejected at preprocess with 'missing field M in main.T': the deploy failed loudly. At head, S returns C.M (line 902 picks the shorter trail), R has been marked visited by the X walk, and T's direct R embed is pruned. The package clears the go/types gate on AddPackage and MsgRun, deploys, and every call runs C.M instead of R.M, with no error. A realm author gets the wrong method's behaviour with nothing to tell them.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/solo-finder-1-wrongmethod.gno gnovm/tests/files/solo1_wrongmethod.gno; go test -run 'TestFiles/solo1_wrongmethod' -v ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang at head (prints C.M) and with base types.go (panics missing field M); go run the Go twin (prints R.M outer)
candidates.evidence: head Output diff: '-R.M outer -R.M outer +C.M +C.M', with no TypeCheckError diff (go/types accepts). base: 'unexpected panic: main/solo1_wrongmethod.gno:30:10-13: missing field M in main.T'. Go twin: 'R.M outer' twice, exit 0.

candidates.summary: Same pruning mechanism in the other direction: a selector that Go rejects as ambiguous, and that the base rejected, is now accepted by the VM and runs one of the candidates
candidates.failure_scenario: T{A; B}, A{C; X}, X{D}, B{D}; C and D each define M; t.M(). Go has T.A.C.M and T.B.D.M both at depth 2, so it reports 'ambiguous selector t.M'. The base saw C.M and X.D.M inside A as a conflict and rejected with 'missing field M in main.T'. At head, A returns C.M, the X walk has marked D visited, and T.B.D is pruned, so the VM runs C.M. On chain, go/types on AddPackage and MsgRun rejects it first, so only direct VM use without type-checking sees the change. The ADR's 'Unchanged from upstream' line covers the same-type diamond, not this shape.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/solo-finder-1-falseaccept.gno gnovm/tests/files/solo1_falseaccept.gno; go test -run 'TestFiles/solo1_falseaccept' -v ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang at head (prints C.M, TypeCheckError 'ambiguous selector t.M') and with base types.go (panics missing field M)
candidates.evidence: head: Output '+C.M' and TypeCheckError '+main/solo1_falseaccept.gno:30:12: ambiguous selector t.M'. base: 'unexpected panic: main/solo1_falseaccept.gno:30:10-13: missing field M in main.T'. Go: './main.go:32:16: ambiguous selector t.M', exit 1.

candidates.summary: cand is allocated for every matching embedded field, including ones then discarded as deeper or tied; the base allocated only for the first match. This contradicts the ADR's 'no extra allocation'
candidates.failure_scenario: A struct with k embedded fields that each promote n builds k trail slices per lookup where the base built one. Each selector resolution at preprocess does k-1 extra Go heap allocations. The cost is small and bounded by MaxStructFields, but the ADR states there are none. Comparing len(trail2)+1 against len(trail) before building cand restores one allocation per winner.
candidates.verify_by: read types.go:899-911: 'cand := append([]ValuePath{vp}, trail2...)' runs before the switch, and the base built the slice only in its 'remember' branch
